content.title: How to use this one presentation
steps: This file contains all user roles. You do not need another guide, a ZIP file or a folder of screenshots to read it.
Read the common steps first. Then use Contents to open the section for the work you have actually been assigned.
The screenshots use practice details. Your own names, records and menus may look different. Use approved practice material when trying a task.
content.result: Use the PDF for easy reading on a phone or computer. The PowerPoint contains the same slides.
content.tip: Never publish, remove accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Sign in to your own account
steps: Open the Luo Heritage address supplied by your organisation. Choose Sign in or Log in.
Enter your email and password, then choose Log in. Check your spelling if it fails.
Community members may also use Google. Staff should use the account supplied by their administrator.
content.result: Your account or dashboard opens.
content.tip: Never share your password. Use only an address you trust.

content.title: Forgot your password?
steps: On the sign-in screen, choose Forgotten password? Select Reset password.
Enter your account email. Choose Send email, then check your inbox and spam folder.
Open the newest reset link within 30 minutes. A link can be used only once.
content.result: An account email arrives if the address is eligible and the email service is available.
content.tip: If no email arrives, contact the person who manages your account. Do not keep requesting links.

content.title: Choose a new password
steps: Open the password reset link from your own inbox.
Enter a new password of at least 12 characters. A short phrase with several words is easier to remember.
Choose Confirm. Return to sign in and use the new password on each device.
content.result: The password changes and old sign-ins are ended.
content.tip: Do not forward the reset link. If it has expired, request a new one.

content.title: Use the library on a phone
steps: Open a collection, such as Muma (Dictionary), from the menu.
Use the picture, headphones, video or page icon to choose a type of content. The four-square icon shows all types.
Choose the list or grid button to change the view. Scroll the entries below the controls.
content.result: The collection shows entries matching your chosen filter.
content.tip: An empty result can mean there are no published entries of that type. Try All.

content.title: Find your access and saved chats
steps: Open the account menu and choose My account & saved chats.
Read My access to check your assigned role. Open a chat from Recent or Archived.
For your name, sessions or notifications, open Profile, sessions & notifications from the menu.
content.result: You can find your own account details and earlier conversations.
content.tip: Choosing an interest such as teacher or researcher does not give staff access.

content.title: Protect your account and other people
steps: Use your own account. Sign out on a shared computer or phone.
Do not copy private interviews, class results or account lists into public chats or messages.
If a screen shows information you should not see, stop and tell the account administrator.
content.result: Your work remains linked to the right person and private information stays protected.
content.tip: Send support the screen name and error message, never your password or a reset link.

content.title: When something does not work
steps: Check your internet connection. Read the message on screen before trying again.
If your sign-in has expired, sign in again. If a button is missing, ask which role and language you have.
If it still fails, note the time, screen, button and exact message. Send these to your account administrator.
content.result: You can explain the problem clearly without exposing private information.
content.tip: Before repeating an upload or submission, check whether the first attempt was already saved.

content.title: How a contribution reaches readers
steps: The uploader or contributor prepares a draft and submits it.
A cultural reviewer checks accuracy. An editor makes requested corrections and returns the item for review.
A publisher checks the final item and permission. Only an approved public release becomes visible to readers.
content.result: An item may return for changes. Drafts and private approvals are not public publication.
content.tip: Different people should perform the independent checks. Do not approve your own work.

content.title: Check permission before sharing
steps: Under Source and access, choose Source permission. If unsure, leave Not sure yet / ask a reviewer.
Choose how to credit the source. Use a person’s name only when they agree.
Keep restricted, sacred or research-only material private. Ask a reviewer before changing access.
content.result: The draft records who may use the material and how the source should be credited.
content.tip: Permission to collect material is not automatically permission to publish it.

content.title: Add pictures, audio or documents
steps: Find Media and transcripts. Choose a file under the matching type.
For an oral history, confirm permission before choosing Start recording. Stop when finished.
Check that the correct files are selected. Keep the app open while an upload is in progress.
content.result: The selected files stay with the contribution when it is saved successfully.
content.tip: If microphone access is refused, allow it in your device settings or attach an existing recording.

content.title: Understand the three save choices
steps: Save on this device keeps a local copy, including selected files. It does not submit your work.
Save private draft saves an online draft for your account. You need a connection.
Submit for reviewer sends the contribution for checking. Wait for confirmation before leaving.
content.result: You know whether the work is on this device, saved online, or sent for review.
content.tip: Clearing browser or app data can remove local drafts. Save again after making changes.

content.title: Open a lesson and keep your progress
steps: Choose Lessons, games & calendar. Open a published lesson.
Read the lesson and answer its questions. Choose Finish & save progress.
Read the result and feedback. Sign in with the same account on another device to keep your learning together.
content.result: You see a saved result or a message saying the attempt is waiting to go online.
content.tip: A score helps you learn; it does not replace a teacher’s review.

content.title: Prepare to study without internet
steps: While connected, open a lesson that allows downloads. Choose Download text for offline use.
Keep using the same browser or app profile. Downloaded text can be read without internet for up to seven days.
Reconnect and choose Refresh & sync. Keep the app open until waiting attempts have been saved online.
content.result: Permitted lesson text is available offline and saved attempts can synchronize later.
content.tip: These downloads contain text, not the audio or video files. Some lessons cannot be downloaded.

content.title: Join a learning course
steps: Open Learning pathways & courses. Choose a published course and read its description.
Open the course and enroll using the button shown. Start with the available lesson.
Use My enrollments to return later. If lessons are locked, complete the earlier lesson and required score first.
content.result: The course appears among your enrollments and shows your lesson progress.
content.tip: If no courses are available, ask your teacher which published course to use.

content.title: Join a class with your teacher’s code
steps: Sign in. Open Teaching & my classes and choose My classes.
Ask your teacher for a current code. Enter it under Join a class, then choose Join class.
Open the class and read its assignments. Use your own account for all submissions.
content.result: Your class appears in My classes.
content.tip: Class codes expire after seven days and may be replaced earlier. Ask for a new code if needed.

content.title: Ask the AI chatbot a clear question
steps: Open Chat or Chatbot. Choose your answer language and read the processing permission notice.
If you agree, allow AI processing. Ask one clear question and wait for the response.
Open any sources provided. Ask a follow-up question if you need a simpler explanation.
content.result: You can read an answer and inspect any linked sources.
content.tip: AI can make mistakes. Do not enter private interviews, passwords or learners’ personal information.

content.title: Community members
steps: You will be able to find cultural material, ask questions and submit your own contribution.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Create a community account
steps: Choose Create new account from the sign-in screen. Enter your name, email and date of birth.
Choose your language and interests. Read and accept the Terms and Privacy Policy.
Set your password and submit. If approval is required, wait for confirmation before signing in.
content.result: Your account is created or clearly marked as awaiting approval.
content.tip: You can choose Google registration if offered, then complete any requested profile information.

content.title: Find your way around
steps: Open the menu on the left. On a phone, use the menu button first.
Choose a collection such as Muma, Ngero or stories. The smaller label explains its content.
Use the same menu for lessons, courses, saved items, contributions and your account.
content.result: You can return to a collection or personal screen without starting again.

content.title: Find a word in the public dictionary
steps: On the public website, open the dictionary page and find its search box.
Enter a Dholuo word or an English or Kiswahili meaning. Wait for the results, then read the relevant entry.
If there is no result, check spelling or try another word. A missing published entry is not proof that the word does not exist.
content.result: You can use the dictionary search where it is offered.
content.tip: The shared app’s Muma screen uses collection filters; it may not show this website search box.

content.title: Read, listen and change the view
steps: Open an entry or choose the grid button, then select its card.
Use See description or See this in English when offered. Audio and video use their own play controls.
Use All if a filter shows no results. Save item is available in signed-in views that offer it.
content.result: You can read the entry and use the media that has actually been published.
content.tip: An unavailable English description does not mean the original entry is missing.

content.title: Return to saved words and items
steps: Sign in and choose Save item on an entry or lesson where that button is available.
Open Saved words & items from the menu. Choose Open collection to return to its source.
Choose Remove saved item when you no longer need the bookmark.
content.result: Your saved list helps you find material again on the same account.
content.tip: Saving a bookmark does not download a file for offline use.

content.title: Update your profile and read notices
steps: Open Profile, sessions & notifications from the menu.
Change your name or interests and choose Save profile. Interests describe you; they do not grant staff duties.
Read your notifications and use Mark read when offered. Check Device sessions if you need to end an old app sign-in.
content.result: Your profile changes are saved and notices are easy to find.
content.tip: Sign out all devices ends your current sign-in too. Sign in again afterwards if you use it.

content.title: Verify your email address
steps: Open account verification and recovery from your account settings.
Choose Verify email under Action, enter your own account email and choose Send email.
Open the newest email link within 30 minutes and choose Confirm. Use a new link if the earlier one has expired.
content.result: The confirmation verifies the address for the intended account.
content.tip: The screenshot shows the same form set to Reset password. Change Action to Verify email for this task.

content.title: If you decide to delete your account
steps: Read the warning first. Deletion removes your sign-in, profile, saved chats and personal progress.
In account recovery, choose Delete account. Request the email link only if you intend to continue.
Open the link and read the confirmation before choosing Confirm. Required cultural-source and review records can be retained.
content.result: You understand the consequences before requesting deletion.
content.tip: This is optional, not a practice task. Active class teachers and the Master Super Admin may need to resolve their responsibilities first.

content.title: Start your own contribution
steps: Choose Contribute & submissions or the Contribute button inside a collection.
Select the collection and choose New private draft. Enter a short title and the requested details.
Use your own material or material you have permission to share. Mark uncertain facts for review.
content.result: A contribution form contains your draft; it is not published.

content.title: What the permission labels mean
steps: Source permission: has the source agreed to the proposed use? Choose Not sure yet when you do not know.
Consent scope: what use was agreed? Public excerpt means an approved public part; research only and teaching have different limits.
Restriction level: who may see it? Internal and restricted are not public. Sacred material needs the collection owner’s special care.
content.result: You understand the labels before you change them.
content.tip: If the permission record is unclear, keep the item private and ask the responsible reviewer.

content.title: Check what happened to your submission
steps: Open Contribute & submissions, then find My online submissions.
Read the status. If asked to make changes, choose Edit draft or requested revision.
Read the reviewer’s request, make the correction, and submit again when ready.
content.result: You can tell the difference between a draft, an item under review and published material.
content.tip: If an item is locked for review, ask the reviewer to return it rather than creating a duplicate.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Find one collection and change its content filter.
Open a lesson or ask a simple AI question, then check any source.
Prepare a private practice draft and identify the option that sends it for review.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Students and learners
steps: You will be able to enroll, join a class, study and find your feedback.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Complete a class assignment
steps: Open your class, then choose Open assignment. Read the instructions and due date.
Choose Study assignment lesson and complete the lesson. Return to the assignment when ready.
Enter the work requested and use the submission button shown. Wait for a saved confirmation.
content.result: Your assignment shows your submission rather than an unsaved answer.
content.tip: If the assignment is closed or the lesson unavailable, contact your teacher; do not submit to a different class.

content.title: Read feedback and try again
steps: Open the same class assignment after your teacher reviews it.
Choose Refresh assignment and feedback. Read the score and the teacher’s comments.
If a new submission is requested and allowed, correct your work and submit it again.
content.result: You know what to improve and which result belongs to you.
content.tip: Sending revised written work clears its previous teacher grade so the teacher can review it again.

content.title: Keep your own learning record
steps: Use the same account on your phone and computer.
Before changing devices, reconnect and use Refresh & sync for waiting attempts.
Do not leave a class just to change devices: leaving can delete your work in that class.
content.result: Your work stays linked to the intended account.
content.tip: Tell your teacher if you accidentally created two accounts.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Enroll in the course your teacher names and open its first available lesson.
Join your class with a current code and find the assignment instructions.
Save one practice result and show where you would read teacher feedback.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Teachers and lecturers
steps: You will be able to run a class and help students find their work and feedback.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Check that you have teaching access
steps: Sign in with your own account. Open Teaching & my classes.
Look for Create class or an existing class where your role is teacher.
If these are missing, ask the language administrator to assign teaching access. Selecting teacher as an interest does not grant it.
content.result: You know whether you can teach a class or are viewing as a learner.

content.title: Create a teaching class
steps: Open My classes and choose Create class.
Enter the class title and requested details. Select a published course if the class needs one.
Choose Save teaching class. Keep the new class join code private until you invite learners.
content.result: The class opens and you can see its invitation controls.
content.tip: Teaching a class does not automatically let you publish cultural content or courses.

content.title: Invite your learners safely
steps: Open the class and find Class invitations. Share its current join code with the intended learners.
Ask learners to sign in and use Join a class. Check the member list afterwards.
If a code is shared too widely, choose Replace class join code or Disable class join code.
content.result: The correct learners are listed in the class.
content.tip: Codes expire after seven days. A replacement invalidates the previous code.

content.title: Set a useful assignment
steps: Open the class and choose Create assignment.
Choose an available published lesson. Write a clear title, instructions and due date.
Choose Save class assignment. Open it again to check exactly what learners will see.
content.result: The assignment is listed for members of this class.
content.tip: Use a lesson in the correct language. If a lesson is withdrawn, choose an approved replacement.

content.title: Review a learner’s submission
steps: Open the class assignment and choose the learner’s submission.
Read their work, enter the score and write feedback that explains one clear next step.
Choose Save teacher grade and feedback. Ask for another submission when correction is needed.
content.result: The learner can refresh the assignment to see the saved grade and feedback.
content.tip: Check the learner’s name before saving. Do not discuss individual results in public chats.

content.title: See the class gradebook
steps: Open the class and choose View gradebook.
Read the assignment columns and learner rows. A teacher’s grade takes priority over a synchronized lesson score.
Use Export gradebook CSV only if you are allowed to keep a spreadsheet copy. Store it privately.
content.result: You can identify submitted, ungraded and completed work.
content.tip: A downloaded gradebook contains personal information. Do not share it as a public attachment.

content.title: Manage changes without losing work
steps: Use Edit assignment before closing submissions. Read any warning when changing instructions.
Choose Close submissions when no more work should be accepted.
Remove a class member only after checking the consequences: that action can remove their class submissions.
content.result: Class membership and assignment availability match your intention.

content.title: Share teaching responsibility
steps: Open the class and find Assign a teacher by existing account email.
Check the colleague’s exact account email and grant teaching access only if you have permission.
Confirm their role in the member list. Keep at least one teacher in each active class.
content.result: The intended colleague has teaching access to this class.
content.tip: A class teacher is different from a system administrator.

content.title: Finish a term or close a class
steps: Save any permitted reports before closing the class.
Choose Archive class only when teaching, invitations and submissions should end. Read the confirmation.
Explain to learners that archived classes remain readable to existing members, while new activity is closed.
content.result: The class is archived rather than accidentally deleted.
content.tip: Do not leave or remove the last teacher from an active class.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Open a practice class and explain how a student joins it.
Identify Create assignment, the feedback area and View gradebook.
Explain the difference between closing submissions, archiving a class and removing a learner.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Uploaders
steps: You will be able to add the right material, record permission and follow its review status.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Open your uploading workspace
steps: Sign in using the account supplied to you. Open the admin dashboard.
Choose Upload Content. Work only in the language assigned to you.
If no collection can be created, check your assigned language with the administrator.
content.result: Your content list opens for the languages you are allowed to upload.
content.tip: Uploaders normally see Dashboard and Upload Content. Other duties require a separate assignment.

content.title: Prepare before you upload
steps: Check the collection, language, title and file names before starting.
Confirm who supplied the material and what permission was given. Keep evidence through the organisation’s approved process.
Use a draft when a meaning, translation or permission is uncertain. Do not guess.
content.result: You have the information needed for a useful draft.

content.title: Enter the contribution details
steps: Open the appropriate new-content form from Upload Content.
Enter the title and all required collection fields. Read the text again for missing words.
Add a clear description and choose Save draft. An admin upload is a draft until submitted for review.
content.result: The online draft appears in your content list.
content.tip: Admin forms use Save draft or Save changes. Community forms use Save private draft and Submit for reviewer.

content.title: What the permission labels mean
steps: Source permission: has the source agreed to the proposed use? Choose Not sure yet when you do not know.
Consent scope: what use was agreed? Public excerpt means an approved public part; research only and teaching have different limits.
Restriction level: who may see it? Internal and restricted are not public. Sacred material needs the collection owner’s special care.
content.result: You understand the labels before you change them.
content.tip: If the permission record is unclear, keep the item private and ask the responsible reviewer.

content.title: Add collection details when required
steps: Open the extra source or collection details section.
Record the known collection date, source reference, location and collector. Leave unknown details for review.
Do not put personal phone numbers, sacred site coordinates or private participant details in a public description.
content.result: Reviewers can understand where the material came from without exposing private details.

content.title: Know where your draft is saved
steps: In Upload Content, Save draft or Save changes saves the item online. Wait for confirmation and check the list.
The community Contribute & submissions form also offers device copies. That is a separate route from the admin upload form.
A device copy is never submitted automatically. To send an admin draft, use Send to cultural review in the online list.
content.result: You know which copy is saved and which action sends it for review.
content.tip: Keep the original file until the online item and its attachments have been checked.

content.title: Send the online draft for cultural review
steps: Return to Upload Content and find the saved draft.
Choose Send to cultural review beside the intended item. Send it only once.
Refresh the list and check its status. You cannot publish an item using only the uploader role.
content.result: The draft is marked as submitted or under review.
content.tip: The English version link opens a separate translation. Complete it where required before review.

content.title: Respond to a correction request
steps: Find the returned item and read the reviewer’s notes.
Open the editable draft, make only the necessary corrections and save.
Submit the corrected item again or follow the editor’s handover. Tell the reviewer what changed.
content.result: The corrected version is ready for another independent check.
content.tip: Editors use Editor Queue. Uploaders use the editable items available in Upload Content.

content.title: Check files before you finish
steps: Reopen the saved item and inspect every attached file.
If an upload failed, reconnect and check whether the text or file was already saved before retrying.
Keep your original source file until the organisation confirms it is safely stored.
content.result: The item has the intended files and no accidental duplicate uploads.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Locate your assigned collection and create a private practice draft.
Explain the permission setting you would choose when permission is uncertain.
Show where you would submit the draft, and explain why you cannot publish it yourself.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Cultural reviewers
steps: You will be able to make a clear, independent cultural review decision.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Open the right review item
steps: Choose Cultural Review in your staff menu.
Open a submitted item in your assigned language. Check that you did not prepare the material yourself.
Read its source, access settings, full text and attached media before deciding.
content.result: You are reviewing the current version of the intended item.
content.tip: An item can change while another reviewer works on it. Refresh if the system asks you to.

content.title: Complete the cultural checks
steps: Open Cultural Review and choose the item. Read its text, source details and attached files.
Check spelling, translation, grammar, pronunciation, examples and cultural context. Tick only what you have checked.
Add useful notes. If the item is correct, choose Approve & Send to Publisher.
content.result: The item moves to the publisher queue after a successful cultural review.
content.tip: If you cannot check a recording or meaning, ask for help rather than ticking the box.

content.title: What the permission labels mean
steps: Source permission: has the source agreed to the proposed use? Choose Not sure yet when you do not know.
Consent scope: what use was agreed? Public excerpt means an approved public part; research only and teaching have different limits.
Restriction level: who may see it? Internal and restricted are not public. Sacred material needs the collection owner’s special care.
content.result: You understand the labels before you change them.
content.tip: If the permission record is unclear, keep the item private and ask the responsible reviewer.

content.title: Request an editor’s correction
steps: Describe the problem in the notes: say where it is, why it matters and what needs checking.
Choose Request Editor Changes when a correction is needed.
The editor fixes the draft and sends it back to cultural review. Check the corrected version again.
content.result: The editor receives a clear change request; the item is not published.
content.tip: Write useful comments such as “Check the meaning in paragraph two,” rather than “Wrong.”

content.title: Raise a serious cultural concern
steps: If material may be culturally false or harmful, explain your concern in the notes.
Choose Propose rejection for reviewer vote. This asks other assigned reviewers to check it.
Do not treat your proposal as a completed rejection. Wait for the required independent votes.
content.result: The concern goes to an independent review vote.
content.tip: For a serious privacy problem, also contact the responsible administrator promptly.

content.title: Vote on another reviewer’s proposal
steps: Open the proposed cultural rejection. Read the reason and the original source.
If you are eligible, choose whether the item is culturally valid or invalid. Give a clear reason for an invalid vote.
Check the confirmation and vote count. You cannot vote on your own proposal or vote twice.
content.result: Your independent vote is recorded. The system applies the required threshold.

content.title: Keep a useful review history
steps: Open Review History to find your recorded actions.
Use the item’s title and review notes when explaining a decision to an editor or coordinator.
If an error is found later, report it with the item reference rather than editing history or concealing the earlier decision.
content.result: Other staff can understand how the decision was reached.

content.title: Review learning material with the same care
steps: Open Lessons, games & calendar if your role offers the content workspace.
Read a submitted lesson, its questions, answers, source and audience. Use the review action only if independently assigned.
A course review is separate from reviewing its individual lessons. Ask the coordinator if the action is not available.
content.result: Learning material receives the appropriate independent checks.
content.tip: A role that can review material does not automatically let its author approve their own work.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Explain one checklist item using an approved practice contribution.
Describe how to request an editor change and how the item returns to you.
Explain why a proposed rejection needs independent votes.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Content editors
steps: You will be able to correct content without bypassing the review process.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Correct an item returned by a reviewer
steps: Open Editor Queue. Find the item and choose Edit details.
Read the requested changes. Correct the text or files, then save your changes.
Return to the queue and choose Send to cultural review. The reviewer must check the corrected version.
content.result: The corrected item returns to cultural review.
content.tip: Saving an edit does not publish it. Keep the source’s meaning and credit.

content.title: Make a careful edit
steps: Read the reviewer’s request before changing the draft. Keep the original meaning.
Correct spelling, formatting, descriptions and the requested collection details. Do not invent missing translations.
Save changes, reopen the item and check that the corrected version is shown.
content.result: The saved draft reflects the requested correction.
content.tip: For a disputed meaning, ask a cultural reviewer rather than silently replacing it.

content.title: What the permission labels mean
steps: Source permission: has the source agreed to the proposed use? Choose Not sure yet when you do not know.
Consent scope: what use was agreed? Public excerpt means an approved public part; research only and teaching have different limits.
Restriction level: who may see it? Internal and restricted are not public. Sacred material needs the collection owner’s special care.
content.result: You understand the labels before you change them.
content.tip: If the permission record is unclear, keep the item private and ask the responsible reviewer.

content.title: Return the item to the reviewer
steps: Go back to Editor Queue after saving your changes.
Choose Send to cultural review beside the intended item.
Read the success message. The item should leave the editable queue when the handover succeeds.
content.result: The current corrected version is ready for cultural review.
content.tip: If the item has already moved, refresh instead of sending a stale copy.

content.title: Prepare a lesson or game draft
steps: Open Lessons, games & calendar and use Content workspace when offered.
Choose Create content. Write the title, content, level and audience; add checked questions and answers.
Save the private draft and submit for independent review. Do not approve your own resource.
content.result: The resource is a draft or submitted item, not automatically public.
content.tip: A written question game is different from a live multiplayer game.

content.title: Build a course from approved lessons
steps: Open Learning pathways & courses and enable Course staff workspace.
Choose Create course. Use published lessons from the same language, place them in order and set required scores.
Save course draft, open it and submit it for independent course review.
content.result: The course draft links the intended approved lessons.
content.tip: Changing a published course requires another review before publication.

content.title: Avoid duplicate or unfinished corrections
steps: If saving fails, keep the draft open and check the connection.
Reopen or refresh only after preserving unsaved text in a trusted place. Check the current item version.
If another person has already changed the item, read their changes before trying again.
content.result: You update the intended current version and avoid overwriting another person’s work.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Find a practice correction and identify the requested change.
Save a corrected draft and locate Send to cultural review.
Explain why editing, cultural review and publication are separate actions.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Publishers
steps: You will be able to check a reviewed item and distinguish public release from internal approval.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Check carefully before choosing Publish
steps: Open Publishing Queue and read the culturally reviewed item.
Check the text, attached files, source permission and public access settings. Add a note if needed.
Choose Publish only when the item is ready. Read the confirmation: an internal approval can remain private.
content.result: Eligible public material becomes available to readers; internal material remains protected.
content.tip: A Publish button is not permission to release sacred, restricted or research-only material.

content.title: What the permission labels mean
steps: Source permission: has the source agreed to the proposed use? Choose Not sure yet when you do not know.
Consent scope: what use was agreed? Public excerpt means an approved public part; research only and teaching have different limits.
Restriction level: who may see it? Internal and restricted are not public. Sacred material needs the collection owner’s special care.
content.result: You understand the labels before you change them.
content.tip: If the permission record is unclear, keep the item private and ask the responsible reviewer.

content.title: Use a final pre-publication check
steps: Confirm the title, language and current version are correct and the cultural review is complete.
Open the files and read descriptions, translations and source credit. Check that public sharing is actually permitted.
If anything is unclear, stop and contact the reviewer or language administrator before publishing.
content.result: The release decision is based on the complete item and its permission evidence.

content.title: Understand the confirmation message
steps: After choosing Publish, read the full success message.
Public release means eligible readers can see the item. Internal curation means it remains private.
Do not change consent or access merely to make an internally approved item appear in the public library.
content.result: You know whether the item was publicly released or privately curated.

content.title: Check the reader’s view
steps: Open the public library, preferably in a separate signed-out browser window.
Choose the correct collection and content type. Find the released item and try its files.
If it is missing, confirm the release message, language, permission and selected filter before escalating.
content.result: The intended public item is readable and its files are usable.
content.tip: Do not test private content by sharing a staff-only link with a member of the public.

content.title: Keep the publication record
steps: Open Published History to find earlier releases.
Record any concern with the item’s title and reference, and notify the language administrator.
If an urgent rights or privacy issue is found, request the approved withdrawal process. Do not assume a saved edit removes a public item.
content.result: Publication decisions and later concerns can be traced.

content.title: Publish lessons and courses separately
steps: In the learning content workspace, inspect validated resources and use publish only when permitted.
For a course, open its staff view and choose Publish course after independent review.
Confirm that both the course and its linked lessons are available to the intended learners.
content.result: Learners see a usable course with available lessons.
content.tip: You cannot independently approve a resource you authored yourself.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Explain the checks you make before Publish.
Distinguish a public release from an internal approval.
Find the public collection and explain how you would report an incorrect release.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Language administrators
steps: You will be able to manage your language’s work while keeping staff duties clear.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Read your language workspace
steps: Open the admin dashboard and confirm the selected language.
Use Content, Cultural Review, Editor Queue and Publishing Queue to find work at each stage.
Use Media, Users and Transcripts only for the material and people in your permitted scope.
content.result: You can direct a question to the right screen and staff member.

content.title: Help users without changing the wrong account
steps: Open Users. Find the person by their own name and email.
Open their details and check their language and current access before changing anything.
Use only the changes allowed by your role. Read every confirmation before suspending or activating accounts.
content.result: The intended account has the correct status and access.
content.tip: Do not select every account to solve a problem affecting one person.

content.title: Give a person only the access they need
steps: Open the person’s account details and verify their email.
Use the role controls available to you for your language. If staff creation is not offered, ask a Super Admin.
Confirm the assignment in the person’s access list and ask them to sign in again if the menu has not refreshed.
content.result: The right person can do their assigned task in the intended language.
content.tip: Language access does not allow you to grant Super Admin ownership.

content.title: Coordinate a review without skipping stages
steps: Check the oldest waiting items and who is assigned to each stage.
Ask the uploader to complete missing source details, the reviewer to check accuracy, or the editor to make requested changes.
Keep independent review: broad access does not make it appropriate to approve your own submission.
content.result: Work moves through the intended people and checks.

content.title: Complete the cultural checks
steps: Open Cultural Review and choose the item. Read its text, source details and attached files.
Check spelling, translation, grammar, pronunciation, examples and cultural context. Tick only what you have checked.
Add useful notes. If the item is correct, choose Approve & Send to Publisher.
content.result: The item moves to the publisher queue after a successful cultural review.
content.tip: If you cannot check a recording or meaning, ask for help rather than ticking the box.

content.title: Correct an item returned by a reviewer
steps: Open Editor Queue. Find the item and choose Edit details.
Read the requested changes. Correct the text or files, then save your changes.
Return to the queue and choose Send to cultural review. The reviewer must check the corrected version.
content.result: The corrected item returns to cultural review.
content.tip: Saving an edit does not publish it. Keep the source’s meaning and credit.

content.title: Check carefully before choosing Publish
steps: Open Publishing Queue and read the culturally reviewed item.
Check the text, attached files, source permission and public access settings. Add a note if needed.
Choose Publish only when the item is ready. Read the confirmation: an internal approval can remain private.
content.result: Eligible public material becomes available to readers; internal material remains protected.
content.tip: A Publish button is not permission to release sacred, restricted or research-only material.

content.title: Check media and translation quality
steps: Open Media and the relevant content item. Check files, labels and access settings.
Use Translations to review the language labels and available translations. Missing text needs a checked translation.
Ask the responsible content editor or reviewer to correct inaccurate material.
content.result: The collection is usable in the intended language without misleading labels.

content.title: Handle teaching access and learning content
steps: Confirm that a teacher has been given actual teaching access; an interest on their profile is not enough.
Check that lessons and courses are published only after independent review.
Ask teachers to handle class membership, assignments and gradebooks within their classes.
content.result: Teachers can use the right classes and learners can open approved lessons.

content.title: Read activity and AI reports carefully
steps: Open Analytics for the activity recorded by the system.
Use AI Monitoring to review recorded questions, feedback and concerns within your allowed access.
Treat low counts as a reason to investigate usage, not as proof of a technical fault. Escalate private-data or accuracy concerns.
content.result: You can explain recorded activity without inventing missing results.

content.title: Handle a permission or privacy complaint
steps: Note the affected item and what the person says is wrong. Avoid copying the private content into your report.
Notify the responsible institutional owner and arrange the permitted restriction or withdrawal action.
Check that the final public view matches the decision and retain the review record.
content.result: A concern has an owner and a documented response.
content.tip: Do not resolve a complaint by silently removing source evidence or review history.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Name the person responsible for each stage of a contribution.
Check a practice account’s language and duties without granting extra power.
Explain how you would handle a missing teacher button or a privacy complaint.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Super Admins
steps: You will be able to coordinate access and monitor work without confusing oversight with editorial permission.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Understand your wider menu
steps: Use Workflow and Library to inspect content, people and collections.
Use Insights to see Analytics, AI Monitoring and Audit Logs.
Administration contains Languages, Admins, Backup and System. Visibility does not mean every action is allowed.
content.result: You can find the right area without assuming that every visible button is yours to use.

content.title: Know the limits of Super Admin access
steps: You oversee the languages assigned to you and may create permitted staff within that scope.
Editing, cultural review, uploading and publishing still require their assigned language duties.
Only the Master Super Admin can create or remove Super Admin authority. Database backups are also reserved for that owner.
content.result: You know when to act and when to refer the request to the Master Super Admin.

content.title: Create a staff account for the right person
steps: Open Admins, then choose + Add Admin. Confirm the person’s email and name.
Choose only the role and language the person needs. Set a strong temporary password.
Save the account. Share access details privately with that person and ask them to set their own password.
content.result: The staff member appears in Administrators with the intended role and language.
content.tip: Only the Master Super Admin can create or remove Super Admin authority.

content.title: Help users without changing the wrong account
steps: Open Users. Find the person by their own name and email.
Open their details and check their language and current access before changing anything.
Use only the changes allowed by your role. Read every confirmation before suspending or activating accounts.
content.result: The intended account has the correct status and access.
content.tip: Do not select every account to solve a problem affecting one person.

content.title: Check staff assignments regularly
steps: Open Admins and verify each person’s email, status, language and duty.
If a person changes duties, update access through the permitted controls; do not share another account.
Read every revoke or deactivate confirmation. Revoking staff duties is different from deleting the person’s account.
content.result: Staff have the access needed for current work and no unnecessary authority.

content.title: Help a user regain access
steps: Confirm which email and language they should be using. Do not ask for their password.
Guide them to Forgotten password? and the newest email link. Check whether the account is active.
If password emails are not being delivered, ask the authorised system owner to check Email settings and the test result.
content.result: The user receives the right recovery instructions without exposing their credentials.

content.title: Review activity and recorded decisions
steps: Use Analytics and AI Monitoring to inspect recorded activity and feedback.
Use Audit Logs to see who changed a record or setting and when.
Investigate unexpected changes with the responsible staff member. Do not alter evidence to hide a mistake.
content.result: You can follow a concern to the relevant person and recorded action.

content.title: Use System settings carefully
steps: Open System and read the selected tab before changing anything.
Change only a setting you understand and are authorised to manage. Save the intended group of settings.
Check the result afterwards. For service keys, backup, legal ownership or an unavailable control, contact the Master Super Admin.
content.result: A deliberate saved change has the intended effect.
content.tip: Do not include secret service keys in screenshots, slides, email or support messages.

content.title: Coordinate content and learning concerns
steps: Route incomplete uploads to uploaders, corrections to editors and cultural concerns to reviewers.
Ask the assigned publisher to check release readiness. Do not bypass the independent checks.
For class work, involve the teacher. Keep learner results and research material private.
content.result: The right person handles the issue without excessive access.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Explain the difference between a Super Admin and the Master Super Admin.
Create no live accounts during practice; instead identify the correct role and language in the form.
Find the recovery, monitoring and escalation paths for a reported problem.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Master Super Admin
steps: You will be able to oversee high-impact actions, delegate responsibly and keep the platform’s records safe.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Your role carries overall responsibility
steps: Use your own protected account. Confirm My access shows Master Super Admin.
Keep the organisation’s ownership, support arrangements and recovery contact current.
Delegate ordinary work to named staff; broad access is not a reason to bypass independent review.
content.result: You know which responsibilities must remain with the institutional owner.
content.tip: Check My access on your own account; the screenshot uses a labelled practice account.

content.title: Create or change Super Admin authority
steps: Open Admins, then + Add Admin to prepare a new staff account.
Select Super Admin only for a trusted person with an agreed responsibility. Assign the languages they oversee.
Check the saved account carefully. Read the consequences before revoking or deactivating a Super Admin.
content.result: Only the intended person receives the intended authority.
content.tip: Never create a shared administrator account for a team.

content.title: Create a staff account for the right person
steps: Open Admins, then choose + Add Admin. Confirm the person’s email and name.
Choose only the role and language the person needs. Set a strong temporary password.
Save the account. Share access details privately with that person and ask them to set their own password.
content.result: The staff member appears in Administrators with the intended role and language.
content.tip: Only the Master Super Admin can create or remove Super Admin authority.

content.title: Maintain your staff list
steps: Open Administrators and review each name, email, language and role.
Remove unneeded authority through the permitted controls after confirming ownership of ongoing work.
Keep cultural reviewers, editors and publishers distinct wherever possible. Record the reason for important access changes.
content.result: Current staff responsibilities are clear and former staff cannot retain unwanted access.

content.title: Add a language deliberately
steps: Open Languages and choose + Add Language.
Follow the numbered language setup: enter the code, name and local name, then check the module and administrator choices.
Review the summary before saving. Creating a language does not create reviewed translations or public cultural content.
content.result: The intended language exists with its configuration ready for checked content.

content.title: Review a language before activation
steps: Open Languages and select the language.
Check its labels, assigned staff and collections. Confirm that any public content is reviewed and permitted.
Use the available activation controls only when the organisation agrees it is ready.
content.result: The public language selection reflects your deliberate decision.

content.title: Check account email settings
steps: Open System, then Email. Confirm the approved provider, verified sender address and private service key.
Save the email settings. Choose Send test email to send to your own signed-in account.
Check both the screen result and your inbox. A provider accepting a message is not proof it reached the inbox.
content.result: You have evidence that the account email path is configured and can be tested.
content.tip: Keep keys secret. Password reset cannot send email while provider credentials or sender approval are missing.

content.title: Help with a failed password reset
steps: Confirm Email settings and the test result before asking the user to retry.
Ask the user to request a fresh link, check spam and use the newest link within 30 minutes.
Keep the user’s reset link and new password private. Record the problem without including either.
content.result: The user can follow a safe recovery path once email delivery is available.

content.title: Make and protect a database backup
steps: Open Backup and choose Backup Now when a backup is authorised.
Wait for confirmation, then check the new file in the list. Store any downloaded copy in the organisation’s protected location.
Ask the technical maintainer to verify recovery. A database backup does not contain the actual picture, audio or video files.
content.result: A protected database snapshot is recorded; separate media backup and recovery checks are arranged.
content.tip: Backup files contain sensitive account data. Never attach them to a public message or training exercise.

content.title: Check public terms and support information
steps: Open System and review the General settings and Terms & Privacy tab.
Replace draft organisation details with the verified operator and support information before publishing those texts.
Have the responsible institution approve the wording. Check the public pages after saving.
content.result: Readers can find the correct organisation and support information.
content.tip: Do not publish a legal draft containing bracketed placeholders or unapproved promises.

content.title: Treat AI settings and feedback responsibly
steps: Use API Keys and AI Monitoring only for the services and records you are permitted to manage.
Keep service credentials private. Test ordinary questions without submitting restricted interviews or personal information.
Investigate wrong answers using their sources and feedback. Do not describe untested language or image models as reliable.
content.result: AI support is used with clear source and privacy checks.

content.title: Use maintenance and ownership controls carefully
steps: Before enabling maintenance, tell the affected staff and agree when access will return.
Read each control and confirmation. Confirm the public view afterwards.
Do not delete the Master Super Admin account to transfer responsibility. Arrange the approved institutional ownership process first.
content.result: High-impact changes have an owner, a reason and a checked result.

content.title: Prepare an orderly handover
steps: Give each person their own account, role guide and approved website address.
Keep private service details, backup locations and recovery contacts in a restricted handover record.
Record which service and device checks have actually passed. Treat physical-server migration and store release as separate planned work.
content.result: The next responsible person can operate the system without sharing passwords or guessing what was tested.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Identify which duties you may delegate and which require Master Super Admin authority.
Explain how to check account email delivery without sharing a key or reset link.
Explain what the database backup includes, what it excludes, and how you would request a recovery check.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Researchers and institutional readers
steps: You will be able to distinguish public reading from authorised research access and request help safely.
Read the common steps on slides 4–19 when you need them. Then follow the tasks in this section.
Use only the duties and language assigned to your own account. Choose Contents at the bottom of a slide to return to the role list.
content.result: Read a step, try it, and check the result before moving on.

content.title: Understand your access before you begin
steps: A researcher interest describes your purpose. It does not unlock private interviews or staff screens.
Start with the public library and approved sources available to ordinary accounts.
For internal research material, contact the person responsible for the collection. Use only the access they formally assign.
content.result: You know which material you may use without borrowing another person’s account.
content.tip: Your assigned role and language determine which records you may open.

content.title: Find a word in the public dictionary
steps: On the public website, open the dictionary page and find its search box.
Enter a Dholuo word or an English or Kiswahili meaning. Wait for the results, then read the relevant entry.
If there is no result, check spelling or try another word. A missing published entry is not proof that the word does not exist.
content.result: You can use the dictionary search where it is offered.
content.tip: The shared app’s Muma screen uses collection filters; it may not show this website search box.

content.title: Use a source, not only an AI answer
steps: Open the approved entry and read its description, language and source credit.
For an AI answer, open the cited platform entries and compare the answer with them.
Record the source title and permitted reference details for your research notes. Follow the organisation’s citation and reuse rules.
content.result: Your notes refer to actual approved material rather than an uncited generated answer.

content.title: Request private research access properly
steps: Describe your research purpose, the collection needed and who will use it.
Ask the person responsible for the collection what permission, consent and access conditions apply.
Wait for approval. Do not treat a visible title, an imported file or a colleague’s copy as permission to reuse it.
content.result: The access request can be considered by the responsible person.
content.tip: Research-only, teaching and public sharing are different permissions.

content.title: For authorised reviewers: open transcripts
steps: This step applies only if you have separately been assigned a role that can read the internal transcript library.
Open Transcripts from the staff menu. Choose the permitted session in your assigned language.
Check the session reference and read only the material allowed by your approval.
content.result: An authorised reader reaches the correct internal session.
content.tip: If Transcripts is missing or access is refused, ask the custodian. Do not try another user’s login.

content.title: Read transcript sections carefully
steps: Open the permitted session and choose a segment, or Expand all segments.
Keep the source reference with your notes. An AI summary is not a replacement for the original text.
Do not translate, publish, export or submit internal text to an external AI service without the required permission.
content.result: Your work retains its connection to the permitted original source.

content.title: What the permission labels mean
steps: Source permission: has the source agreed to the proposed use? Choose Not sure yet when you do not know.
Consent scope: what use was agreed? Public excerpt means an approved public part; research only and teaching have different limits.
Restriction level: who may see it? Internal and restricted are not public. Sacred material needs the collection owner’s special care.
content.result: You understand the labels before you change them.
content.tip: If the permission record is unclear, keep the item private and ask the responsible reviewer.

content.title: Request an export rather than assuming permission
steps: Tell the collection owner exactly which records and fields are needed and why.
Ask for the approved export and any citation, storage, sharing or deletion conditions.
Check the files and permission record together. Keep participant identities and sensitive locations protected.
content.result: Any research copy has a documented purpose and agreed conditions.
content.tip: An administrator’s technical ability to export is not the same as permission for your study.

content.title: Report a source or consent concern
steps: Note the item title and reference, and describe the concern without copying restricted text.
Contact the person responsible for the collection or the administrator who granted your access.
Pause any disputed reuse until the responsible person confirms what is permitted.
content.result: The rights concern is handled without spreading the disputed material.

content.title: Check your skills before working alone
steps: Find a public source and explain how you would cite it.
Explain why the researcher interest does not grant internal access.
Describe how you would request a transcript or dataset export and check its reuse conditions.
content.result: You are ready for routine work when you can complete these steps without help.
content.tip: Use only approved practice material. Do not publish, delete accounts or change live settings just to practise.

content.title: Finish confidently and ask for help
steps: Keep this one file. Return to Contents whenever you need another task or role.
If a screen is empty, access is refused or a service is unavailable, read the message and contact the person who manages your account.
Give support the screen name, button and message. Never send your password, a reset link or private research material.
content.result: Use your own account and follow the conditions attached to every source.
